sources.title: NZFC: New Zealand Screen Production Rebate, Criteria for New Zealand Productions, 1 July 2026 v.1.0
sources.said: The New Zealand Rebate is 40% of QNZPE. The New Zealand Rebate is capped at $12 million per production. … a series or season of a series whether scripted or unscripted including but not limited to drama, documentary, factual, reality, children’s and animation being a programme with a common theme or themes consisting of at least two episodes that are intended for release together in a national market or markets. Each episode (with the exception of animation) must be a least one commercial half-hour in length; or … Series of programmes – scripted … $1 million total and no less than $500,000 per hour … $10 million total per season … The proportion of non-New Zealand Government Production Funding for a television or other non-feature film production must be 25% of the Production Budget or higher. … A television or other non-feature film production must achieve 20 points or more (including the minimum points required in sections A and C) in the Significant New Zealand Content Test.

sources.title: NZFC: Rebate for New Zealand Productions
sources.said: Series - Scripted … NZ$1 million total … and at least NZ$500,000 per hour … or NZ$10 million per season … Other formats: At least 25% non-NZ government funding and 10% market attachments.

sources.title: NZ On Air: Round Rua Information for Funding Applicants, 12 August 2026
sources.said: Scripted … Approximately $8m available. … Projects seeking between $1m and $3m … We expect our contribution to NZSPR projects to be no more than $3m per project.

sources.title: NZ On Air: General Guidelines for Applicants (updated July 2026)
sources.said: Applications seeking 100% NZ On Air funding will only be successful in very exceptional … Platform cash contribution to the production budget … This is our preferred option.

sources.title: NZ On Air: Karere newsletter, April 2026 (Round Toru 2025/26 decisions)
sources.said: We received 108 applications from 83 applicants requesting total funding of approximately $52m and we were able to support approximately 44% of projects that applied. … Round Toru was open to Scripted applications for drama and comedy, including partial financing of feature films. We received 10 applications for Scripted funding and have committed just over $8m to three Scripted projects in this round.

sources.title: NZ On Air: Round Tahi 2025 Scripted funding decisions (1 August 2025)
sources.said: $9million was allocated in this round for Scripted projects, with priority being given to those accessing the Screen Production Rebate in the interests of encouraging third party investment and creating ambitious content that delivers to local and international audiences. Ten applications were received seeking close to $22million. … Luminous Beast, who co-produced After The Party, have been funded for a new comedy drama, titled All Of Me. … Returning for a second season is the comedy musical series Happiness … Also returning in 2026 is Aotearoa’s longest-running soap Shortland Street . … Rounding out the Scripted projects funded is Day One Shorts 2026

sources.title: NZ On Air Investment Model 2026
sources.said: Scripted and Non-fiction projects seeking completion funding without securing platform investment.

sources.title: Creative New Zealand: Creative Impact Fund
sources.said: Artists and practitioners who are New Zealand citizens or Permanent Residents. … Arts organisations and groups can not apply to this fund. … You can apply for up to $125,000. … Most grants will be less than $100,000. … If you apply for more than $50,000, you must show in your budget that you have revenue from other sources.

sources.title: Creative NZ: Creative Impact Fund 2026 - Round 1 (results posted 20 May 2026)
sources.said: 27 applications have been offered funding of $825,016 to make, share, and present work that enriches audiences and communities, encouraging understanding and participation. We received 247 eligible applications with $10,729,419 requested. … 6 – Theatre

sources.title: Creative NZ: Creative Impact Fund 2025 - Round 2 (results posted 3 December 2025)
sources.said: 36 applications have been offered funding of $1,273,794.25 to make, share, and present work that enriches audiences and communities, encouraging understanding and participation. We received 342 eligible applications with $17,694,349.39 requested. … 3 – Theatre

figures.finding: A New Zealand series (passing the Significant New Zealand Content Test) gets the same 40% as a feature, but its threshold is per hour of the production (total QNZPE over its duration in hours), or NZ$10m for a season. Every half-hour and hour episode the game makes clears the half-hour minimum. International productions get 20% (+5% points test) under separate criteria not re-read here.

value.distribution: a secure confirmed commercial agreement for NZ distribution on an appropriate platform

figures.finding: A NZ series is commissioned before it is made (platform attached at application; completion funding without platform investment is ineligible), so a 'pickup after the shoot' rate does not apply as the UK model has it. No count found.
